summary.text: A male child with short bowel syndrome after massive intestinal resection at 5 days of age for midgut volvulus with malrotation had 9 cm of residual small bowel with the ileocecal valve and entire colon preserved. He was placed on home parenteral nutrition and referred to the reporting hospital at age 2, where PN volume and calories were adjusted and synbiotics, a proton pump inhibitor and oral supplements were started. Seven catheter-related bloodstream infections occurred before TED initiation, and pneumatosis intestinalis developed at age 5 and recurred at age 6.

At age 5 he was enrolled in a teduglutide clinical trial and later continued commercially for more than 6 years, with a baseline PN volume of 42.4 ml/kg/day and 27.5 kcal/kg/day. A fecal occult blood test before TED was negative, and colonoscopies about 6 months and 1 year after TED initiation found no polyps and led to a diagnosis of eosinophilic gastroenteritis or gastrointestinal disorder, treated with montelukast with no further recurrence.

PN volume was reduced by more than 20% by three years, fat emulsion was cut by about 50% and later stopped, and he was completely weaned from PN after 6 years of treatment. TED was temporarily stopped twice and resumed. Growth stayed stable, laboratory values showed no remarkable changes, adverse events were 23 before and 17 after TED initiation, and no severe TED-related adverse events were reported.
